antiguo-seminario-mayor-de-comillas.summary: After the first Marquis died on 17 January 1883, his son Claudio López Bru had the plans drawn up, and the first stone was laid on 20 May 1883. The design was by Catalan architect Joan Martorell i Montells, who worked for the marquis in Barcelona and on the Sobrellano complex in Comillas. The Seminary belongs to late-19th-century Historicism, using Gothic and Mudéjar styles, then considered the true Spanish architecture. The visit can be combined with the Palacio and Chapel-Pantheon of Sobrellano; if buying online, leave at least 90–120 minutes between the two start times. Private parking costs €2, with €1 off for Seminary visitors.

casa-de-los-abades.summary: Probably built at the end of the 17th century, this house originally belonged to the abbots of the Colegiata. Today it is known as the Casa de la Archiduquesa, having been the residence of Archduchess Margarita of Austria-Bourbon. The coats of arms are modern, made by local artist Jesús Otero, and show the emblems of Santillana's most notable lineages (Barreda, Velarde, Cossío, Villa, Bracho, Peredo and others), with the archduchess's arms beside them.

casa-del-duque-de-almodovar-del-rio.summary: Designed at the end of the 19th century by Francisco Hernández Rubio for the Prado de San José, this house takes its name from Swiss chalets and its forms from the much-admired English architecture, stressing every typical feature of those supposedly rustic styles: asymmetry, multiple axes, and woodwork and brickwork. It contrasts with the eclecticism of the Palacio de Sobrellano and the Modernisme of Gaudí's Capricho.

cementerio-modernista-de-comillas.summary: Comillas cemetery has an original Modernista front: a round arch flanked by small paired columns and crowned by a decorated cornice, with a highly ornamental iron gate. A rubble-stone wall topped with decorative pinnacles encloses it, all designed by Domènech. The cemetery reuses the late-Gothic parish church (late 15th–early 16th century), whose ruin is crowned by a marble angel by sculptor Josep Llimona i Bruguera. Some notable mausoleums survive, above all the Piélago family's, designed by Domènech and made by Llimona. It is reached via the approaches to the harbour and beach from the centre of Comillas.

centro-cultural-el-espolon.summary: In the late 18th century Juan Domingo González de la Reguera, Archbishop of Lima and a native of Comillas, had El Espolón built to house a Chair of Latin Grammar, established by royal decree of King Charles IV in 1789; in 1802 the Real Seminario Cántabro was founded here. Designed by architect Cosme Antonio Bustamante, it was restored in 2009 by Peridis. It now hosts cultural tourism, training, workshops, associations, a library and a telecentre; note its central courtyard and temporary exhibitions. Nearby are the Plaza de la Constitución (old town hall, San Cristóbal church), the Plaza del Corro, the Fuente de los Tres Caños and the Sacred Heart monument.

colegiata-de-santa-juliana.summary: The Colegiata de Santa Juliana grew out of the expansion of the earlier monastery of the same name in the mid-12th century. It was founded by a group of monks to help repopulate the area, with a small hermitage to display the relics of the martyr Juliana that they had brought with them. The village took the monastery's name, "Sancta Iuliana", which evolved into today's Santillana. Its high altarpiece, made between the late 15th and early 16th centuries, blends Flamboyant Gothic and Plateresque elements. Declared a Site of Cultural Interest (BIC) in 1889.

el-capricho-de-gaudi.summary: Originally named Villa Quijano, El Capricho is one of the most representative works of Spanish Modernisme. Designed by the Catalan architect Antoni Gaudí and built in 1883–1885, it is one of his very few buildings outside Catalonia. It was commissioned as a summer house by Máximo Díaz de Quijano, a music-loving indiano enriched in Cuba and brother-in-law of the Marquis of Comillas. Music runs through it: iron railings shaped like treble clefs and semiquavers, and tubular window counterweights that chimed like bells. Bands of exposed brick alternate with sunflower-tile friezes, porch capitals show palm leaves and swallows, and the Persian-minaret-style tower blends Arab, Mudéjar and Gothic influences.

monumento-al-marques-de-comillas.summary: Raised by the town of Comillas in memory of Antonio López y López, whose economic and social rise after returning from Cuba and setting up his businesses in Barcelona culminated in 1878, when Alfonso XII made him Marquis of his native Comillas in recognition of his financial and material support against the Cuban insurrection. It stands on a meadow that López's friend Ángel Pérez gave to the town for the monument. Cascante's design, respected by Domènech, has an original ship's-prow pedestal and a column carrying the marquis's statue. Maritime themes abound, and its bronze statues of allegories of the Antilles and the Philippines were especially notable.

museo-de-altamira.summary: The museum lies 2 km from the centre of Santillana del Mar. Its history starts with a management board set up in 1924. The first building serving the cave was a traditional mountain house for displaying and conserving finds from the excavations and housing the first guard. Rising visitor numbers led to three pavilions in the 1970s, and in 1979 the Ministry of Culture created the National Museum and Research Centre of Altamira to better manage and conserve the cave. The current building by architect Juan Navarro Baldeweg opened in 2001, its siting and design driven by protecting the cave. It is a state museum of the Ministry of Culture and Sport.

museo-diocesano-regina-coeli.summary: Housed in the former Dominican friary of Regina Coeli ("Queen of Heaven"), the museum holds over 800 works from parishes across the region, notable for their popular character and dominated by sculpture, which with stonemasonry was the region's traditional craft. Besides the iconography of popular local saints, it shows Flemish, American and Castilian (mainly Burgos and Valladolid) influences of the Baroque era. Highlights include Gothic sculpture, the San Roque and San Sebastián groups, Hispano-Philippine silks and ivories, enamels and silverwork, especially from America. It also studies and catalogues the Diocese of Santander's heritage and, with the regional government, opens about 50 religious monuments free of charge.

museo-jesus-otero.summary: Sculptor Jesús Otero Oreña left his legacy to his home town in this museum and foundation beside the Colegiata de Santa Juliana. Opened in 1994 with works he donated in 1993, it holds about fifty sculptures, many from his last years, plus the tools, implements and drawings he used. Born in Santillana in 1908, Otero first exhibited in a group show in Santander; a scholarship holder at the San Fernando Academy of Fine Arts, he was strongly influenced by Emiliano Barral and Victorio Macho. Months before his death he donated all his remaining works, and friends and admirers set up the museum in the former Guardia Civil barracks and workshop-school.

palacio-de-peredo-barreda.summary: One of the town's most elegant and singular buildings, the ensemble comprises the palace, its annexed houses and their splendid garden. It stands on an older Gothic tower or house of the Barreda family and was built around 1700 by Francisco Miguel de Peredo, whose lineage also owned the palaces of Mijares and Viveda. It is also called the Palacio de los Benemejís, as descendants of the Marchioness of Benemejís owned it until Caja Cantabria bought it. A modern cultural centre in the adjoining Velarde and Quijano houses runs a regular exhibition programme, and the restored palace, with its library and decorative and fine arts collections, is a new cultural space.

palacio-y-capilla-panteon-de-sobrellano.summary: Joan Martorell designed the Palacio de Sobrellano and its Chapel-Pantheon for the first Marquis of Comillas, Antonio López López, as a summer residence for the Marquis and the royal family: a neo-Gothic jewel with a Modernista aesthetic. The palace, begun in 1882 after the chapel, opened years after the second Marquis died. Octagonal, it has a central hall, a monumental stone staircase and a great salon with eight panels painted by Llorens. The chapel, a cathedral in miniature, has the pantheon below, a seat, prie-dieux and benches by Gaudí, paintings by Llorens and Masdeu, sculpture by Joan Roig and marble tombs by Llimona and Vallmitjana. BIC since 1981. The Chapel-Pantheon is closed for restoration.

playa-de-san-juan-de-la-canal.summary: A beach on the coast near Santander, 1 km from Soto de la Marina. It is well known for the busy party held nearby on the night of San Juan. Length 580 m; fine golden sand; deep slope; gentle drop.

puerto-de-comillas-el-muelle.summary: Comillas men seem to have taken up fishing on a significant scale only in the 16th century, because San Vicente de la Barquera held the exclusive right to fish the coast for two leagues east and west of its harbour. The oldest known ordinances of the Comillas fishermen's guild, the Cofradía de Pescadores del Santo Cristo del Amparo, date from 1522 and were revised in 1611. In the 17th century Comillas became the whaling capital of the Cantabrian Sea, and this wealth paid for its picturesque quays, its splendid parish church and its town hall.

zoo-de-santillana.summary: Covering 60,000 m², this private zoo has been rated by ADENA/WWF one of the four best zoos in Spain. It focuses on four main attractions: primates, big cats, tropical butterflies and waterfowl. Its 30,000 m² Parque Cuaternario themed area takes visitors back 14,000 years to when Altamira's people roamed these lands, with European bison, reindeer, Iberian wolves, roe deer, bears, deer, Przewalski's horses, European otters, capercaillie and a wide collection of northern waterfowl.
